They are again tossed about as lovers of sin and having become apostates from Israel, very wicked and bitter in their counsels, not through God. For it is not lawful to take counsel with God, for those who wish to agree with some of the wicked. But one who is pious and good and a lover of righteousness will take counsel with God and will turn to practical things. For it is written that 'the thoughts of the righteous are judgments.' Therefore, they accuse the chosen Israel, as having introduced a mind apostate from God concerning Christ. For they were inquiring, gathered together, and said: 'What do we do, since this man performs many signs? If we let him be, the Romans will come and take away your city and your land.' Another of the leaders said: 'You do not know that it is expedient for one man to die, and not for the whole nation to perish.' The Lord teaches this more clearly, saying in the evangelical parables that 'the householder who planted the vineyard sent his servants to receive the fruits, but the farmers killed them.' And their impieties have not stopped at this.

But they saw the son sent by the father with the servants and said to themselves 'This is the heir, come let us kill him and take his inheritance for ourselves.' They are apostates, introducing sin upon sin, having killed the holy prophets, then also the heir, the son. They had a long-standing intention to apostatize from God, going down to Egypt to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by the Egyptians without asking God. The sequence of thoughts is: woe to those going down to Egypt to be helped by Pharaoh and to find shelter with the Egyptians. For they had been warned of war and battle and the king of Assyria marching against the land of Judah, yet they ran to the Egyptians for help, calling for their assistance, although they should have been appeasing God and turning to better things.
pass_b_english: They are being tossed about again as lovers of sin and having become apostates from Israel, being very wicked and bitter in their counsels, and not through God. For it is not lawful to take counsel with God when one wishes to agree with some of the wicked. But one who is pious, good, and a lover of righteousness will take counsel with God and will turn toward practical things. For it is written, 'The thoughts of the righteous are judgments.'

Therefore, the chosen Israel is being accused, as having introduced a mind apostate from God concerning Christ. For they were inquiring, having gathered together, and said, 'What are we to do, since this man performs many signs? If we let him alone, the Romans will come and take away both your city and your land.' Another of the leaders said, 'You do not know anything, that it is expedient for one man to die, and not for the whole nation to perish.'

The Lord teaches this more clearly by saying in evangelical parables, 'The householder who planted the vineyard sent his own servants to receive the fruits, but the farmers killed them.' And their impieties have not stopped at these things; for having seen the son sent by the father along with the servants, they said to themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and take his inheritance for ourselves.'

Thus, they are apostates, the proponents of such bitter and impious schemes, adding sin upon sin; for they killed the holy prophets, and then also the heir, that is, the son. Because their intention to apostatize from God is seen from afar, they attempt to make it certain by saying: 'Those going down to Egypt—they did not ask me to be a help under Pharaoh, or to be a shelter under the Egyptians.'

The sequence of these thoughts is this: Woe to those going down to Egypt to be helped by Pharaoh and to find shelter among the Egyptians. For having been informed of war and battle and the king of Assyria moving his weapons against the land of Judah, they ran to the Egyptians for help, calling for their assistance, even though they ought to have been appeasing God and turning toward better things.
